what_happened: While reading a config-only request, Athena wrote a criterion (criterion 7) that limited which tests could strip the [job_plan] section from athena.toml. The reader found that other tests (in athena-data's config.rs and athena-core's run_pin_tests.rs) also read the repo's real athena.toml and would need the same change. The repo and defaults did not settle this, so the reader asked the user. The user answered that criterion 7 was too strict. Those tests may also strip the section, no non-test code changes, one shared helper should be used where the crates allow, and every test edit must be named in the design doc's note.
cause: The reading wrote a scope limit from the files the request named, without searching the repo for every consumer of the changed config. Nothing in the reading step finds all the tests that load the real athena.toml. The strict criterion would have blocked a necessary change, and only the reader's check exposed it, after the reading was made.
prevention: When a reading restricts edits for a config-changing job, a check should first list every file in the repo that loads the changed config file (for example by searching for athena.toml reads in tests and code). The reading should then allow test-only edits to all of those files, and bar only non-test code changes. A scope criterion would then be built from the real set of dependents instead of a guessed one, so the reader would not need to ask.
proposed_request: Remove the [job_plan] section from the repository's athena.toml as the design doc describes. Keep the tests passing. Tests that read the real athena.toml may strip the [job_plan] section before parsing. This covers crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs, crates/athena-data/src/config.rs tests, and crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs. Share one stripping helper where the crate dependencies allow it. Change no non-test code under crates/. Name every test edit in the design doc's note.
